To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we constructed and compared eight candidate assemblies combining different DNA sequencing methods and genome assembly algorithms to produce a high quality draft genome of the coral reef fish Pearlscale Pygmny Angelfish; and (2) the best assembly had a scaffold contig N50 127 Mb higher than the assembly obtained using shotgun data only, and was more accurate than any other published fish genome assembly that did not utilize linkage map information.

1) the assembly of the coral fish genome is the most contiguous and accurate fish assembly to date, 2) the use of multiple sequencing methods and assembly algorithms is critical for producing high-quality draft genomes, and 3) the genome of the coral fish is the first fish genome that is complete and contiguous enough to be used as a reference genome for comparative genomics studies.

the best candidate assembly for the Pearlscale pygmy angelfishes genome was obtained by combining four different data types (shotgun reads, long mate-pairs and Chicago libraries) and four different assemblers, and that this best candidate assembly had higher contiguity and completeness than other fish assemblies that did not use linkage maps.

improving the quality of genome assemblies for non-model organisms, which will help to advance the fields of genomics, evolution and conservation.
the development of new methods for genome sequencing and assembly, and the application of these methods to a coral reef fish species of interest.
the assembly and annotation of the first high-quality reference genome for a Pomacanthid fish species.

the assembly is high quality, and that the assembly is the best of its class, and is the best assembly of a fish genome without the use of long-read data.

the combination of different data types, including long-range mate-pair, long-range Chicago and overlapping shotgun sequencing data, and the use of four different assemblers, produced a high-quality draft assembly of the coral Pygmy anglerfish, C. vrolikii.
our best candidate assembly is a highly contiguous and accurate draft genome of the Coral Reef Pearlscale Pyrgmy Angelfish.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a high quality draft genome assembly for the Pearlscale Angelfish, which will serve as a valuable resource for the scientific community.
the combination of long and short read sequencing and assembly algorithms can produce a high-quality de novo assembly of the genome of a coral reef fish.

the best candidate assembly of the Pearlscales Pygmy anglerfish genome was produced using the following combination of sequencing methods and assembly algorithms: 1) Illumina shotgun reads, 2) mate pairs, 3) Chicago reads, and 4) assembly by the hybrid assembler, MaSuRCA, with the addition of a final scaffolding step with SSPACE.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of different data types can produce high-quality draft genomes at lower cost and in less time than using only long-read technologies.
it is possible to obtain a high-quality draft assembly using a combination of overlapping short-read data, mate-paired libraries and the Chicago library method.
a combination of short-read shotgun sequencing, mate-pair libraries and Chicago libraries is a cost-effective way to produce high-quality draft genome assemblies of fish.
